claim_under_test: The compiler could not name THE REGION of the page a word picks out. It could list 107 elements; it could not say 'that row, and the trash inside it'. That inability -- not any missing app state -- is what produced the MULTI_APP refusals, and naming the region converts those pages.

the_wrong_answer_this_replaces.label: REFUSED__MULTI_APP_STATE_OUTSIDE_OBSERVATION
the_wrong_answer_this_replaces.why_it_was_believed: the instruction named an app (email, contacts, calendar) and the observation showed a page, so 'the state lives outside the observation' was a plausible sentence.
the_wrong_answer_this_replaces.what_dumping_the_page_showed: on email-inbox the observation carries 107 elements including div.email-sender 'Enrichetta', div.email-subject, div.email-body and div.email-actions holding span.trash and span.star. Nothing was outside the observation. The machine had no way to SAY which of the 107 a word picked out, so it reported the absence of a name as the absence of a state.
the_wrong_answer_this_replaces.generalisation: this is the third round in a row where a refusal label aimed engineering at the world when the defect was in the language. A refusal is a work list, and a work list that names the wrong thing is worse than no work list.

what_was_built.idea: A frame is (container, identifier, path_from_id): a coordinate change instead of a vocabulary entry. One implementation serves every record-shaped page, because 'the star of that row' is not an email fact.

rules_learned_by_measurement.rule: a frame is the LARGEST container that does not swallow a second record
rules_learned_by_measurement.why: the nearest container holding a control is div.email-left (sender, subject, body) but the star is in the SIBLING div.email-right. Stopping at the nearest one locates the email and then cannot find the control in the same row. Walking further up spans the two halves; the only thing that must stop it is another record's identifier.

rules_learned_by_measurement.rule: a control is named by its OWN text or an EXACT class token, never a prefix
rules_learned_by_measurement.why: email-sender starts with 'email'; a prefix test made the sender's name a control for the word 'email'.

rules_learned_by_measurement.rule: identity uses own text/value/aria/title/alt -- never full_text
rules_learned_by_measurement.why: full_text is the whole subtree, so every ancestor of a name 'showed' the name and one email looked like seven records.

rules_learned_by_measurement.rule: a record that is one page-turn away is a SEARCH, not a missing observable
rules_learned_by_measurement.why: phone-book does not show 'Larissa' and does show a pager; the honest answer is reachable_by, and the repair is paging, not a new channel.

rules_learned_by_measurement.rule: the whole sentence survives the frame
rules_learned_by_measurement.why: the frame answers WHICH RECORD. Returning it alone dropped "Felis massa ac nulla." -- the text to write -- so the email was opened and nothing was sent.

rules_learned_by_measurement.rule: the record is also a THING TO OPEN, and the form behind it names controls by CLASS
rules_learned_by_measurement.why: Reply lives in div.email-send inside the OPENED email; the forward form's send icon is #send-forward with no text at all. Its class/id is the sentence's own verb and the preposition says which field.

rules_learned_by_measurement.rule: read the sentence again against the page that now exists
rules_learned_by_measurement.why: the reply field does not exist until the record opens. Compiling once at time zero dropped the value. This is the same reading applied where it can be done -- not memory: nothing is carried between pages.

measured_effect.why_a_new_instrument: the previous harness lived in /tmp and was lost with the sandbox. A measurement you cannot re-run is a memory, not a result.
measured_effect.reward: read only after the arm stops, and only to record whether it was right
measured_effect.census_reading: 52 won, 51 refused, 27 executed-and-lost. The refused total is HIGHER than the round's starting 44 despite 9 more pages solved, because the instrument was corrected mid-round: it had been counting 16 pages that emitted nothing as 'not refused' and 6 pages with a `refused_part` as having no refusal. A measurement that under-reports its own refusals is measuring its optimism. MULTI_APP is down from 12 to 1 (+2 half-understood), which is the claim this receipt makes.

laws: a refusal stated before the evidence is not caution, it is a bug that looks like discipline
the frame answers WHICH RECORD, and it does not answer WHAT ELSE THE SENTENCE SAID
a control is what it says it is; a class prefix is not a name
a record that is not on screen is a search to run, not an observable to build
read the sentence again against the page that now exists, and remember nothing
an index captured at compile time is not an action -- the page renumbers between observations

corrections.claim: 12 pages were refused because the app's state lives outside the observation
corrections.status: FALSE. 11 of 12 were one row away. MULTI_APP was a statement about the vocabulary.

corrections.claim: a bridge action is written {kind: click, index: n}
corrections.status: FALSE. It is {type: click, index: n}. Three probe rounds reported 'the page does not change on a click' because every click was UNKNOWN_ACTION. The page changed the whole time (37 -> 24 elements).
FALSE. 'Reply' is the words under the icon; the control is #send-reply (or span.email-reply), and the forward form's send icon has no text at all.

corrections.claim: 43/130 with 44 refusals was an honest census
corrections.status: FALSE. The instrument counted a page that emitted no action and carried no refusal label as neither refused nor failing, and counted a half-understood instruction (`refused_part`) as not refused. 16 + 6 pages were invisible. Corrected before the next measurement.

corrections.claim: "Click the button." is an instruction that cannot be understood
corrections.status: FALSE, and a test asserted it for months. The page states tag='button' on exactly one element. CLICK_KIND existed with a checker and had no producer. It is now produced -- last, after every path that names or describes a target, because putting it first cost 12 pages that were already solved.

corrections.claim: the first capitalised word of an instruction is a name
corrections.status: FALSE. 'Use the terminal' made 'Use' a record and 'Switch between the tabs' made 'Switch' one. A capital at a sentence start is capitalised because of where it is; the rule is positional, not a vocabulary of verbs to skip.

tests.provenance: captured by this project's own chromium bridge against the real pages at seed 1060 on 2026-11-16; no synthetic observation is used

honest_limits: 52 of 130 is capability on these pages at this seed with a 30-action budget. It is not a benchmark claim and not a family rank.

51 pages are refused and 27 more execute without reward. The largest named groups are NO_CLAUSE_UNDERSTOOD (10) and THE_ARM_CANNOT_ACT (9), and the second is a new, honest name for what used to be invisible.
daily-calendar still refuses under MULTI_APP, where that label is true: an interval plus a named event is calendar semantics, not a frame.
the drag pages (drag-box, drag-shapes, drag-shapes-2) still compile and dispatch and do not register reward; that defect is untouched.

the four choose-date pages and use-autocomplete emit one action and lose; they are likely a DOM-events defect (selecting a value without dispatching what the widget listens for), which is a hypothesis, not a measurement.
